title: brynko-pulse configuration
description: The merged configuration: pulse.yaml, channels.yaml and every file in monitors/.

server_address.description: How people reach this server, shown in alerts beside server_name, for example 203.0.113.10 or web-1.example.com.
How people reach this server, shown in alerts beside server_name, for example 203.0.113.10 or web-1.example.com.

id.description: Stable identifier: lowercase letters, digits, - and _.

envRef.description: Secrets are never written here: write ${NAME} and put NAME=value in secrets.env.

phoneList.description: Phone numbers in international format, for example +919876543210.

notify.description: Channels for monitors that set none.

for.description: How long a problem must last before alerting.

cooldown.description: How often to repeat an alert while the problem continues.

interval.description: How often each monitor is checked.

flapping.description: A monitor that changes state this many times within the window is marked flapping and sends one alert instead of many.

maintenanceList.description: Weekly windows during which alerts are held back, as with pulse silence.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone such as Asia/Kolkata. Default: the server's local time.

monitors.description: Monitor ids the window applies to. Default: every monitor.

clock.description: A time of day as HH:MM, 24-hour, for example 02:30.

max_alerts_per_minute.description: Above this, alerts are folded into one summary message.

command_output_bytes.description: Output kept from a command check.

max_heals_per_hour.description: Self-healing attempts allowed per hour across all monitors on this server. Above this, pulse stops trying and alerts.

api.description: Local API for tools and a future UI. Never listens on a network port.

watchdog.description: Dead-server alert through the brynko relay: pulse checks in every minute, and the relay alerts you when this server stops checking in (it is down, cut off, or pulse stopped). Off unless set. pulse sends the server's name and address, its version, and the email addresses and WhatsApp numbers of the channels it alerts; nothing about your monitors.

key.description: This server's relay key, as a ${NAME} reference to secrets.env.

notify.description: Email channels whose addresses the relay alerts. Other channel types are skipped: their addresses hold secrets that never leave the server. Empty: the server's default channels (defaults.notify).

url.description: Where to check in: an https:// address. Leave it unset for the brynko relay.

type.description: Where the alert goes; each type adds its own fields below.

min_severity.description: Send only alerts at or above this severity.

language.description: The template's language code, for example en or en_US.

url.description: Must start with http:// or https://.

api_key.description: This server's brynko key, as a ${NAME} reference to secrets.env. The app sets it up for you.

whatsapp.description: WhatsApp numbers in international format, for example +919876543210.

url.description: Where the relay takes alerts: an https:// address. Leave it unset.

heal.description: Self-healing: what pulse does when this monitor fails. In ask mode pulse prepares the fix and waits for you to approve it; in auto mode it runs the fix by itself. Either way it waits until the problem has lasted the monitor's for (at least 30s), runs the steps in order, and waits verify for the monitor to be OK again.

mode.description: ask: prepare the fix and wait for approval (pulse fix approve, or the app). auto: run it by itself; after 2 automatic fixes that did not help in one problem, or when the tries are used up, the next fix waits for approval. off: keep the rule but do nothing.

steps.description: What to do, in order. pulse stops at the first step that fails.

only_if_ok.description: Monitors that must be OK before a fix. When one of them is failing, it is the likely cause: pulse does not fix this one and says so in the alert.

timeout.description: How long all the steps together may take.

attempts.description: How many automatic fixes within the window. Fixes you approve are not counted.

within.description: The window automatic fixes are counted in.

verify.description: How long to wait after a fix for the monitor to be OK again before counting it as not helping.

healStep.description: One step: restart services, restart containers, or run a program.

restart_service.description: Services to restart, in order: on Linux systemd units without .service, on Windows service names. pulse gets the right to restart only these.

restart_container.description: Docker containers to restart, in order, by name as docker ps shows it.

run.description: A program and its arguments. Never run through a shell; it runs as the pulse service account.

id.description: Unique name, used by status, history, silences and ping.

type.description: What to watch; each type adds its own fields below.

name.description: Shown in alerts and lists. Empty: the id.

enabled.description: Off keeps the monitor in its file but stops checking it.

interval.description: How often pulse measures it. Types that follow events (containers, services, files, logs) also notice a change at once; this is the regular check in between. Empty: the server's default (defaults.interval).

alert_when.description: The comparison that means something is wrong. Some types have a default.

clear_when.description: When the problem counts as over, and pulse sends a resolved message. Set a lower level than the alert (alert above 85%, back to normal below 80%) so it does not flip back and forth around one value. Empty: as soon as alert_when is no longer true.

for.description: How long the problem must last before you are alerted, so a short spike does not wake anyone. Empty: the server's default (defaults.for), or at once when it sets none.

severity.description: How serious an alert is. Empty: the server's default (defaults.severity).

notify.description: Channels told about this monitor. Empty: the server's default channels (defaults.notify).

cooldown.description: While the problem lasts, the alert is sent again this often, until it is over. Empty: the server's default (defaults.cooldown).

path.description: A filesystem's mount point, or any path on it, for example / or /data (on Windows D:\).

service.description: The service name, for example nginx: on Linux the systemd unit without .service, on Windows the service name.

container.description: The container name, as docker ps shows it.

match.description: The process name exactly as ps shows it, for example nginx. On Linux a process whose command line contains it also counts.

host.description: Where to connect. Empty: this server (127.0.0.1).

url.description: Must start with http:// or https://.

method.description: GET for pages and most APIs.

expect_status.description: Status codes that count as up, for example 200, or 200 and 301. Empty: any 2xx or 3xx.

body_contains.description: Text the answer must contain. pulse reads the answer as text (up to 1 MB) and looks for this exactly as written, capitals included, for example "status":"ok".

json_path.description: For a JSON answer: the field to read, for example status, data.state or items.0.name (a number picks a list item). Alert on its value with json_value (a number or text), or on whether it is there with json_found.

json_expect.description: The value the JSON field must have, as a comparison: == ok, != error, > 0. When set, a different value counts as not answering as expected. Text is compared with == or != only; quote a number to compare it as text.

follow_redirects.description: Follow redirects to the final page.

host.description: A host name with an optional port, for example example.com:443.

file.description: Or a certificate file on this server, for example /etc/ssl/certs/site.pem.

source.description: Exactly one of: file (a path), journal (a systemd unit, or empty for the whole journal), eventlog (a Windows channel such as Application).

pattern.description: A regular expression; a line that contains a match counts.

window.description: matches counts the lines that matched within this time.

path.description: The file to watch, for example /var/backups/db.sql.gz.

run.description: The program and its arguments. Never run through a shell.

parse.description: What to read: only the exit code, the output as text, or the output as a number (it must start with one).

expect_every.description: How often the job runs, for example 1d for a nightly job.

grace.description: Extra time allowed before it counts as late.
